hints: Recall that distance travelled on a velocity-time graph is represented by the area between the graph and the time axis.
Calculate the area of the trapezium formed from $t = 0$ to $t = 10$ with parallel sides 10 s and 6 s, and height $0.9\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
Use the property that distance travelled equals the area under the velocity-time graph:
$$\text{Distance} = \text{Area of trapezium from } t = 0 \text{ to } t = 10$$
$$\text{Distance} = \frac{1}{2}(a + b)h = \frac{1}{2}(10 + 6)(0.9)$$
$$\text{Distance} = \frac{1}{2}(16)(0.9) = 8 \times 0.9 = 7.2\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Name the foundational graphical principle: the distance travelled by a particle is equal to the area under its velocity-time graph.

Over the interval from $t = 0$ to $t = 10\text{ s}$, the graph forms a trapezium with parallel horizontal bases along the time axis ($10\text{ s}$) and at constant speed ($9 - 3 = 6\text{ s}$), with height $0.9\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Write the area formula for a trapezium:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{a + b}{2} \times h$$
$$\text{Distance} = \frac{10 + 6}{2} \times 0.9$$

hints: Notice that because the particle returns to $O$, its net displacement from $t = 10$ to $t = T = 12$ must be $-7.2\text{ m}$.
Represent the displacement from $t = 10$ to $t = 12$ as the signed area of the triangle below the time axis: $\frac{1}{2}(12 - 10) v_{\text{min}}$.
Solve $\frac{1}{2}(2) v_{\text{min}} = -7.2$ to find the minimum velocity.
walkthrough:
Use the condition that the particle returns to $O$ at $T = 12\text{ s}$, meaning the signed area below the axis equals $-7.2\text{ m}$:
$$\text{Displacement} = \frac{1}{2}(T - 10)v_{\text{min}} = -7.2$$
$$\frac{1}{2}(12 - 10)v_{\text{min}} = -7.2$$

Solve for the minimum velocity $v_{\text{min}}$:
$$\frac{1}{2}(2)v_{\text{min}} = -7.2 \implies v_{\text{min}} = -7.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the physical condition: the particle returns to its starting point $O$ at time $T = 12\text{ s}$. Therefore, the backward displacement in the return journey must exactly cancel the forward displacement of $7.2\text{ m}$ gained in the first $10\text{ s}$:
$$\Delta s_{\text{return}} = -7.2\text{ m}$$

The return journey is represented by a triangular region below the time axis from $t = 10$ to $t = 12\text{ s}$. The base is:
$$\text{Base} = 12 - 10 = 2\text{ s}$$

Set up the signed area equation for this triangle:
$$\text{Signed Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{Base} \times v_{\text{min}}$$
$$\frac{1}{2}(2)v_{\text{min}} = -7.2$$

hints: Notice that greatest speed $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$ occurs during the return motion, where the triangular area below the axis equals $7.2\text{ m}$.
Form the equation $\frac{1}{2}(T - 10)(3) = 7.2$ to solve for the return duration and find $T = 14.8\text{ s}$.
Calculate the total distance travelled over the whole motion as $7.2 + 7.2 = 14.4\text{ m}$.
Divide the total distance by total time $T = 14.8\text{ s}$ to determine the average speed as an exact fraction.
walkthrough:
Set up the return journey area using the maximum speed of $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find $T$:
$$\frac{1}{2}(T - 10)(3) = 7.2$$
$$1.5(T - 10) = 7.2$$
$$T - 10 = \frac{7.2}{1.5} = 4.8 \implies T = 14.8\text{ s}$$

Calculate the total distance travelled over the entire motion:
$$\text{Total distance} = 7.2 + 7.2 = 14.4\text{ m}$$

Calculate the average speed for the whole motion:
$$\text{Average speed} = \frac{\text{Total distance}}{\text{Total time}} = \frac{14.4}{14.8} = \frac{36}{37}\text{ m s}^{-1}\quad (\approx 0.973\text{ m s}^{-1})$$
teacher_walkthrough: Identify that because the forward speed peaked at $0.9\text{ m s}^{-1}$, the greatest speed of $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$ must occur during the return journey below the time axis.

The area of the return triangle must equal the total backward distance of $7.2\text{ m}$ to bring the particle back to $O$:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$$
$$\frac{1}{2}(T - 10)(3) = 7.2$$

Multiply through by 2 and solve for $T$:
$$3(T - 10) = 14.4$$
$$T - 10 = \frac{14.4}{3} = 4.8$$
$$T = 10 + 4.8 = 14.8\text{ s}$$

State the definition of average speed as total distance divided by total time elapsed:
$$\text{Average speed} = \frac{\text{Total distance}}{\text{Total time}}$$

The particle travels $7.2\text{ m}$ forwards and $7.2\text{ m}$ backwards:
$$\text{Total distance} = 7.2 + 7.2 = 14.4\text{ m}$$
$$\text{Average speed} = \frac{14.4}{14.8}$$

Simplify the fraction by multiplying numerator and denominator by 10 and dividing by 4:
$$\frac{144}{148} = \frac{36}{37}\text{ m s}^{-1}\quad (\approx 0.973\text{ m s}^{-1})$$
